title: Iman Gadzhi's CLEAR method: ranking 5 AI side hustles (UGC, websites, clipping, voice agents, digital products)
summary: Iman breaks down five AI side hustles with pricing, retainer math and pros and cons, then scores each with his CLEAR framework (competition, longevity, effort, autonomy, recurring). AI digital products rank first because income decouples from hours. Voice agents rank second because a steep learning curve thins competition and clients stay sticky.

principles.text: Analysis paralysis is the real blocker. People who pick one option and start beat those who keep researching.
principles.quote: the people who just picked one, they're already ahead. Not because they were smarter than you, but simply because they stopped scrolling, and they just started.

principles.text: Score any business idea with CLEAR: Competition, Longevity, Effort, Autonomy, Recurring, five points each out of 25.
principles.quote: It's called the CLEAR method. CLEAR is an acronym and it stands for competition, longevity, effort, autonomy, as well as recurring.

principles.text: A low barrier to entry is a double-edged sword. It makes starting easy but floods the market and pushes people to compete on price.
principles.quote: when everyone can do the same thing, people start competing on price. And normally, that's a race to the bottom that you don't want to get into.

principles.text: Prefer monthly retainers over one-off projects. Recurring revenue means you don't start at zero every month.
principles.quote: the real money is in the retainers, okay? A brand pays you a flat fee every month for a specific batch of videos.

principles.text: A harder skill is a moat. Fewer people push through the steep learning curve, so competition stays manageable and the service pays more.
principles.quote: I would say this one has the steepest learning curve, but that's also exactly why it pays the most. Fewer people push through the barrier.

principles.text: Sell by showing the cost of the problem, not by persuading. When the ROI is obvious before the pitch ends, selling gets easy.
principles.quote: instead of trying to convince them, instead you're showing them what it's already costing them not to have it.
